questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to design a beautiful home
Why children are always untidy
How to sell unwanted things online
Why clutter affects us and how to get rid of it
questions.why: They discuss the problem of clutter and hear advice on decluttering your home.

questions.q: What did the Woman's Hour listener say in her message?
options: She loves collecting things and says clutter has never been a problem
Clutter is harming her mental health, so she's giving herself a week
She paid a professional to tidy her house
She throws everything away at 4 a.m. every day
questions.why: She says clutter is affecting her mental health, woke her at 4 a.m., and she's given herself a week.

questions.q: What does Neil say about clutter in his home?
options: He is the untidiest person in his family and leaves things everywhere
He enjoys having lots of things around
His children make a mess everywhere and it annoys him
He recently threw everything away
questions.why: Neil lives with children, says there is clutter everywhere, and 'it drives me mad'.

options: As a minimalist who doesn't own much
As someone who can't throw things away
As a professional organiser
As someone who tidies every morning
questions.why: Georgie says she's a minimalist and doesn't have very much stuff.

questions.q: According to TV judge Michelle Ogundehin, why can clutter make us tired?
options: Our brains have to work extra hard to process the mess around us
We spend too much of our free time cleaning and tidying it every day
It stops us sleeping at night
It makes our homes too hot
questions.why: She says our brains are constantly processing our surroundings, so they 'work overtime' in chaos.

questions.q: Which reasons are given for why people put off decluttering?
options: It's expensive and needs special tools
Their families won't let them
It takes time and deciding what to keep is emotional
They don't know where to take the rubbish or who can collect it
questions.why: Georgie says it takes time and it can be emotionally disturbing deciding what to keep.

questions.q: What is organiser Ingrid Jansen's main advice?
options: Clear the whole house in one weekend
Do it slowly, one drawer or cupboard at a time
Ask a friend or relative to decide what you should throw away
Buy more storage boxes first
questions.why: She says you have to declutter 'slowly but surely: one drawer, one cupboard at a time'.

questions.q: Why does Ingrid describe people who try to sort out a whole room in one weekend?
options: To show that this is the quickest method
To praise their energy and enthusiasm
To explain why weekends are the best time to do this kind of job
To show that doing too much at once often makes more chaos
questions.why: She says after two hours they find 'more chaos than there was before'.
